title: Engineering
subtitle: Diagnostics, Repair and Systems Control
intro: Engineering keeps the Cori running when systems fail, power fluctuates, or technical problems suddenly become the main character of a mission. This is where analysis, repairs, improvisation, and the ability to stay clear-headed under pressure matter most.
roleText: Engineering ensures that the Cori remains operational and mission-ready. This includes system stability, power distribution, repairs, technical safety, and supporting other departments during scientific or tactical situations.
workflowSteps: Analyze the cause and identify affected systems
Secure ship systems and set priorities
Carry out repairs or implement a workaround
Verify functionality and document the incident
missionExamples: Recalibration of sensor or power distribution systems
systemsItems: EPS network and emergency power routes
Internal ship systems and maintenance access points
coordinationItems: Science for sensors, scans, and technical analysis
Ops and Command for power priorities and system authorization
Security during damage control situations and critical infrastructure failures
Medical for life support, environmental systems, and emergencies
cultureText: Engineering on the Cori means pragmatic thinking, clean logic, and staying calm in chaos. If you enjoy breaking problems apart, understanding systems, and dealing with technical mission work, this is where you belong.
projectsItems: Diagnostic protocols for recurring system faults
Technical mission reports and damage analysis
Improving internal maintenance and response procedures
Supporting scientific missions through technical evaluation
newcomerText: No one is expected to know every system detail from day one. What matters is an interest in technology, logical thinking, and the ability to approach problems in a structured way.
noteText: Engineering on the Cori does not operate by the motto of hope and duct tape, even if both occasionally help. The goal is understandable, credible, and creative problem-solving with attention to systems, interdependencies, and consequences.
